applies_why: The judge text resolves D5 vs C5 by treating CR2 G's answer to the challenger's rows as leaving the sign's sense open, which is the kind of verse-level open-sense determination K-C governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'never verse by verse'—read either as barring any link resolution from the open sense of one verse and requiring chain-by-footing, or as barring only express contrary-verse counting while still allowing open-sense underdetermination; I used the former.
why: Because the judge declares D5 underdetermined from the open sense left by the almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows rather than comparing the challenger's chain with CR2 G by footing, it breaches K-C.
